decision: KEEP TypeScript and native HTML buttons/details for explicit bounded host-session controls after source-based reassessment; block Start during synchronous source withdrawal as well as while a session is pending.
constraints: Offline browser ESM component with English/Swedish control and state guidance, native buttons and no credential fields or persistent state.

One host operation at a time; start returns only after cleanup. Stop, permission withdrawal and page suspension synchronously invoke source withdrawal and abort the owned signal. No queued start or automatic reconnect.
Default disabled; host grants UI availability while server and host remain responsible for actual authorization. No new service contract, peer module or native iOS work.

A reentrant host callback cannot start a session while disconnect is executing. Such Start actions are ignored, never queued; a later explicit Start remains available after successful withdrawal and host enablement.

alternatives.assessment: Selected: two native buttons, one status region and local details guidance need synchronous state/withdrawal ordering and direct host AbortSignal interoperation. No reactive graph, custom-element registry or extra runtime is needed. Public types expose the required host lifetime contract.
Equivalent runtime behavior is possible. Checked annotations and declarations would still be needed for consumers, with no demonstrated semantic or performance advantage over typed source.

Official lifecycle documentation provides connection/disconnection hooks and asynchronous reactive updates. Reusable custom elements are credible for a larger component system, but this scope needs an explicitly owned root and synchronous withdrawal independent of render scheduling. No custom-element integration requirement establishes a material win.

Ports, flags and custom elements support JavaScript integration while isolating application state. An Elm application could govern a larger UI; this component must interoperate with the existing native AbortSignal and synchronous source-clear contract through JavaScript regardless. No separate application state model is required here.

Typed external bindings support native JavaScript functions and DOM integration. A viable alternative, but the present two-action lifetime contract has no cross-module representation or sharing requirement that materially benefits from another compiler boundary.

limits: Host callbacks are trusted application code: disconnect must synchronously clear the source and refresh its display; start must cover the entire session and cleanup, honoring the provided abort signal. A nonsettling callback keeps the start gate closed.

setEnabled is a UI availability hint, not an authorization mechanism. The containing application and backend must enforce permissions. UI text intentionally says requested, never authenticated or connected.

The containing application synchronizes locales across components and owns account workflows. Seven contextual topics cover only these controls, not the full P19 Help Center or release-SHA coverage inventory.
Native HTML and structural DOM tests do not prove actual browser keyboard, screen-reader, contrast or installed-product acceptance. No native performance or cross-language speed benchmark claimed.
No tactical, actuation, targeting, identity history, cryptographic, availability or production qualification.
Reentrancy guards prevent overlapping callback work in the component; they do not contain arbitrary host code or prevent it from starting independent operations outside this interface.
